issues.body:
Both assertions in this test are negative (`!set.contains(&[x, p, x])`, `!set.contains(&[y, p, y])`). Confirmed by grep that the reasoner has no owl:ReflexiveProperty handling anywhere in crates/sparq-reason/src -- the symbol appears only in this new test -- so both assertions hold trivially today. They would also continue to hold if `materialize_owl_rl` regressed into a complete no-op, or bailed out early on this input: the input triples are `[p, rdf:type, owl:ReflexiveProperty]` and `[x, p, y]`, neither of which is `[x, p, x]` or `[y, p, y]`. Additionally, eq-ref sameAs pairs are only emitted for non-singleton equality classes (owl.rs:1734-1743) and this input creates none, so the output vec plausibly equals the input vec verbatim -- the test cannot observe whether the reasoner ran at all.

So the test pins the intended guard but cannot distinguish "OWL-RL correctly declines to add reflexive edges" from "OWL-RL did nothing". Kept at minor, not major, for the same reasons as round 1: it still has real value as a regression guard against someone later adding a ReflexiveObjectProperty rule that does not belong in the RL profile, it produces no false green for any currently-implemented behavior, and the companion test in the same commit (`sameas_and_inverse_functional`) does exercise the production path and was confirmed mutation-red. This is a re-raise of the identical round-1 finding at the identical severity -- it was not addressed by the round-1 CI-repair commit, which only rewrote the sameAs IRI construction.
issues.title: reflexive_property_does_not_materialize_self_edges is still a pure negative test with no positive control (unchanged from round 1)

verdict.summary:
Test-only change to crates/sparq-reason/src/owl.rs adding two unit tests inside `mod tests`; no production code is touched. The round-2 delta vs round 1 is one line: `&format!("{}sameAs", OWL)` -> a hoisted `let same_as = [OWL, "sameAs"].concat();`. Semantically identical (both yield "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#sameAs"); it is a clippy `uninlined_format_args` repair and introduces no defect.

Verified empirically at the PR head:
- `cargo test -p sparq-reason --lib`: 144 passed, 0 failed; `--features substrate-join`: 151 passed, 0 failed. Green in BOTH feature states, which matters because prp-ifp has cfg-gated branches (owl.rs:1120 default FxHashMap `inc.get`; owl.rs:1124 `adj.probe_inc`) and the test drives both.
- `sameas_and_inverse_functional` is non-vacuous and hits the real production path: the derivation is gated on `if ax.inv_functional.contains(&p)` (owl.rs:1116), and the second assertion (`ex:b ex:p ex:marker`) is reachable only via prp-ifp then eq-rep substitution -- nothing else in the 4-triple input yields it. Round 1's mutation spot-check (`if false && ...` -> RED) still applies since that production code is byte-identical.
- `has()` (owl.rs:2185) fails closed (`si != 0 && pi != 0 && oi != 0 && ...`), so no assertion can pass via an absent IRI.
- The OWL 2 RL claim is accurate: ReflexiveObjectProperty is excluded from OWL 2 RL (prp-irp exists at owl.rs:1852/1907; no ReflexiveProperty rule) and `owl:ReflexiveProperty` is the right term. Grep confirms the crate's only occurrence is this test, so no-self-edges is correct.
- rustfmt is informational, not a gate (ci.yml:5-7, 1231-1233), so the hand-split `has(...)` call is not a gate failure.

Progress is stagnant: round 1 recorded exactly one minor finding (negative reflexive test lacks a positive control); the round-2 CI-repair commit did not address it, so it is re-raised at the same severity. No new findings, nothing higher severity, no blocker/major -- approve.
